questions.statement: A bird has two ________ to fly.
questions.context: Learning about animals' physical characteristics in English class.

options.feedback: A bird does not have human arms; its forelimbs are modified into wings.
Correct. Birds have two wings, the limbs they beat to lift themselves off the ground and fly.
'Legs' are what a bird stands on; they are not what makes it fly.
'Ears' are used for hearing, and birds do not use them to fly.

questions.statement: A fish has ________ to swim in water.
questions.context: Learning about animals' physical characteristics in English class.

options.feedback: A fish has no hair; hair is a covering of mammals.
Correct. Fins are the flat limbs a fish uses to push against the water and move forward.
'Wings' belong to birds and insects, not to fish.
'Hands' are human limbs with fingers, and fish do not have them.

questions.context: Learning about animals' physical characteristics in English class.

options.feedback: A 'fin' is a fish part for swimming, and an elephant has no fins.
A 'feather' covers a bird, not an elephant.
Correct. The trunk is the elephant's long nose, which it uses to breathe, smell and pick things up.
A 'wing' belongs to a bird, not to an elephant.

questions.statement: A cat has long ________ on its face.
questions.context: Learning about animals' physical characteristics in English class.

options.feedback: 'Toes' are at the end of a foot, not on an animal's face.
'Fingers' are human digits used for gripping, not what a cat has on its face.
'Arms' are human limbs; a cat has front legs.
Correct. Whiskers are the long stiff hairs on a cat's face that help it judge narrow spaces.

questions.context: Learning about animals' physical characteristics in English class.

options.feedback: 'Fur' is the hairy coat of mammals such as dogs and cats; birds are not mammals.
Correct. A bird's body is covered in feathers, which are its characteristic outer covering.
'Scales' cover fish and reptiles, not birds.
A bird's skin is thin and mostly hidden under its feathers, so it is not its covering.

questions.context: Learning about animals' physical characteristics in English class.

options.feedback: 'Blue' is not a colour of any real tiger; tigers are orange and black.
Correct. A tiger's fur has orange and black stripes running along its body.
'Spotted' describes a leopard, not a tiger.
'Plain' means with no pattern, and a tiger's fur is clearly patterned with stripes.

questions.context: Learning about animals' physical characteristics in English class.

options.feedback: 'Plain' means without a pattern; a leopard is covered with spots.
'Red' is not the colour of a leopard's coat; its spots are dark on a pale coat.
Correct. A leopard's fur is covered in dark round spots, which is its natural camouflage pattern.
'Striped' describes a tiger or a zebra, whereas a leopard's pattern is made of spots.

questions.statement: A dog has a ________ that it wags when it is happy.
questions.context: Learning about animals' physical characteristics in English class.

options.feedback: A 'trunk' is an elephant's nose, and a dog does not have one.
A 'wing' belongs to a bird, not to a dog.
A 'fin' is a fish part for swimming, and dogs do not have fins.
Correct. A dog's tail is the part it wags from side to side when it is happy.
